title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate ordinaires'. Setup: S_0 is smooth over a perfect field k (affine, S_0 = Spec A_0, if one wishes). S is a formally smooth formal scheme over W = W(k) lifting S_0. F_S is an endomorphism of S that is semilinear over the Witt-vector Frobenius σ and lifts the absolute Frobenius of S_0. In other words, a Dwork-style Frobenius lift.

BTO(S_0) is the category of ordinary Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups over S_0. Grothendieck defines a linear-algebra category C = C_{S,F_S} whose objects are tuples (P', Q', M, ∇, F_M, Fil_0):
- P', Q' are twisted-constant p-adic sheaves, i.e. lisse étale Z_p-local systems on S (equivalently on S_0), locally free of finite type.
- M is an extension 0 → Q'⊗O_S → M → P'⊗O_S → 0.
- ∇ is an integrable connection on M compatible with the extension structure, the outer terms carrying their canonical connections.
- F_M : F_S^*M → M is a horizontal morphism of extensions inducing the canonical iso F_{Q'} on the sub and p·F_{P'} on the quotient. So the sub is the unit-root (slope 0) part and the quotient has slope 1.
- Fil_0 is a splitting of the reduction M_0 (an extension of P'_0⊗O_{S_0} by Q'_0⊗O_{S_0}) compatible with F_{M_0}; a crossed-out note adds it need not respect the connection.

The Dieudonné-module functor D : BTO(S_0)^op → C sends G to its contravariant Dieudonné crystal evaluated on (S, F_S), with:
- Q', P' coming from the Tate modules of the étale and multiplicative parts of the connected–étale sequence, which for ordinary G is an extension of an étale by a multiplicative BT group;
- ∇ the crystal connection;
- F_M the crystalline Frobenius;
- Fil_0 the Hodge filtration on S_0, which is transverse to the unit-root sub.

Question: is D an equivalence of categories? This is the ordinary special case of Grothendieck's 1970 conjecture that Dieudonné theory is fully faithful (or an equivalence) over smooth bases.

The next page starts the analysis. Choosing a splitting φ of M, splittings form a torsor under L ∈ Γ(T⊗O_S) with T = P'^∨⊗Q'. Frobenius has the shape F(x,y) = (px, y + Φx). A change of splitting gives Φ' + F_S^*L = Φ + pL, a Dwork-type twisted cocycle relation. Compatibility with Fil_0 lets one choose L, Φ ≡ 0 on S_0.

In modern terms, ordinary BT groups are extensions of étale by multiplicative groups. These are classified by Ext(P_et, Q_mult), which for a reduced base is roughly lim O^*/O^{*p^n} ⊗ T, and on the Dieudonné side by classes of Φ modulo the image of (p − F_S^*), plus ∇ and Fil. The Kummer/Dwork map ũ ↦ (1/p)log(F_S(ũ)/ũ^p) links the two, as in Katz's Serre–Tate local moduli and Deligne–Illusie's 'cristaux ordinaires et coordonnées canoniques'.
errors: Fil_0 cannot be just any splitting. Compatibility with F_{M_0} forces F_S^*Λ + Φ ≡ 0 mod p (it is the Frobenius descent of ker F_{M_0}, i.e. the Hodge filtration). The page leaves 'compatible à F_{M_0}' unspecified, but the next page uses it correctly.
No topological quasi-nilpotence condition on ∇ is stated, though it is needed for (M,∇) to come from a crystal. Plausibly it is automatic in the presence of F_M; minor gap.
On the next page the matrix written as (id Φ; 0 p·id) does not literally match the formula F(x,y) = (px, y+Φx) as written. This is a notational slip only.

ideas.what: Description of the Dieudonné crystal of an ordinary BT group over smooth S_0 via a Frobenius-lifted formal lift (S, F_S): a unit-root sub F-crystal, a slope-1 quotient, a connection and a mod-p Hodge splitting
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root sub-F-crystal of an ordinary F-crystal; Dwork/Katz description of ordinary crystals with Frobenius lift
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwork; Katz (Travaux de Dwork 1973, Serre–Tate local moduli 1981); Deligne–Illusie 1981
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk and Montréal 1970 lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974); unsure for the ordinary case specifically

ideas.what: Question whether the Dieudonné functor BTO(S_0)^op → C is an equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné-theory equivalence over smooth bases (ordinary case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck (1970); proved in general for smooth bases by de Jong (1995); ordinary case essentially via Katz / Deligne–Illusie
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, ICM Nice 1970; 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

ideas.what: Change-of-splitting relation Φ' + F_S^*L = Φ + pL (next page), classifying the extension by Φ modulo (p − F_S^*)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit Frobenius-lift linear-algebra category for ordinary BT groups over a smooth base, keeping the Hodge filtration only mod p (on S_0) rather than on S. This is a precursor of Deligne–Illusie canonical coordinates and of Faltings/Fontaine–Laffaille-type modules over Frobenius-lifted bases, predating them by about a decade. The equivalence question is left open on this page.
missed.quote: On a un foncteur canonique ("module de Dieudonné") D : BTO(S_0)° → C. Question : Est-ce une équivalence de catégories ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck was working out the ordinary case of his Dieudonné conjecture with Dwork-type Frobenius lifts around 1970. The results themselves were later established by Katz, Deligne–Illusie and de Jong.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early, explicit formulation of the ordinary case of the crystalline Dieudonné equivalence using a Frobenius lift and a mod-p Hodge splitting, anticipating Katz/Deligne–Illusie. However, the conjecture itself is Grothendieck's published 1970 one and the mathematics was later fully developed by others.
transcription_corrections: 'compatible avec σ sur W_k' likely reads 'σ sur W(k)'.
'Fil_0' in the tuple versus 'Fil' later refers to the same datum (a splitting over S_0).
In the F_M section, the struck-out text after 'induisant' is 'sur Q'⊗O_S'; the line reads 'compatible avec les connexions, induisant respectivement F_{Q'} … et pF_{P'} …'.
